parts.text:
15 What is the definition of power?
A
work done in one second
B
work done in unit time
C
work done per second
D
work done per unit time

hints: Notice the four options differ only in two words: in against per, and one second against unit time.
Recall power is a rate given by $P = W/t$, so the wording must mean work divided by time.
Think why a general definition cannot fix the time unit to the second and must use unit time.
walkthrough: Start from the physical meaning: power is the rate of doing work, written as $P = W/t$ where $W$ is work done in joules and $t$ is time taken.
The word per means divided by, so a rate must be phrased as work done per time interval.
The word in only says when the work happens, so work done in one second or in unit time does not state the division $W/t$.
A definition must also be independent of the SI second, so it uses unit time to mean one unit of whatever time scale is used.
Combining division language with unit independence gives work done per unit time. This is option D.

A.explanation: It fixes the time to one second and uses in, which does not express division of work by time.

B.explanation: It uses unit time but the word in does not express a rate as $W/t$.

C.explanation: It uses per to show a rate but fixes the time unit to the second instead of any unit of time.

D.explanation: It correctly states rate as work divided by time, $P = W/t$, for one unit of time.
